findings.title: KeyError when existing integration metadata has no "sender"
findings.body: The new identity check reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` unconditionally. But `build_integration` only adds the `sender` key to metadata when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (lines 376-377), and the existing `test_basic_flow` asserts that a normally-created GitHub integration's metadata has no `sender` key at all. Any integration that was created via the normal Sentry-initiated pipeline (no `sender` in state) and is later re-attached (Integration exists but has no OrganizationIntegration, so this branch runs) will raise `KeyError` and return a 500 instead of the intended "Invalid installation request" error page. The check should guard for a missing/empty sender (e.g. `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")`) and fail closed with the error page.

findings.title: Token exchange / user lookup errors are not caught, producing 500s
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(...)` at line 423 and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` at line 434 are called outside any try/except (only `safe_urlread` is wrapped). `safe_urlopen` raises on non-2xx/network failures and `get_user_info` raises when the `/user` request fails. During a GitHub outage, an invalid/expired token, or a re-used `code`, these will propagate as an unhandled exception and render a 500 rather than the intended `github-integration-failed.html` error page that the PR describes for exactly these failure cases. Wrap these calls so failures deterministically fall through to `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests installation-not-found
findings.body: `test_installation_not_found` stubs the `/app/installations/{id}` endpoint to 404 and expects the old "The GitHub installation could not be found." message. After this PR the second request uses a state value (`ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`) that does not match the pipeline signature, so the flow short-circuits in `OAuthLoginView` at the state check and returns "Invalid installation request." before ever reaching `get_installation_info`. The 404 stub is now dead code and the installation-not-found path (the `IntegrationError` in `build_integration`) is no longer covered by any test, while the test name is misleading. Either drive the request with the correct signature and assert the not-found error, or rename/split the test so both the state-mismatch and installation-not-found behaviors are actually exercised.
